title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse and locality-aware pinning optimizations
author: Anika Rao
description: Motivation: On high-concurrency workloads the paged KV cache suffers from allocator churn and cross-locality cache evictions which increase tail latency and per-token GPU time. This PR implements two complementary improvements: 1) reuse-aware block allocator to avoid repeated allocation/free cycles for hot KV pages, and 2) locality-aware pinning so that hot blocks are preferentially placed and pinned on the same NUMA/GPU-local memory region to reduce cross-device transfers. Summary of changes: - Implement BlockPool that holds reusable Block objects with lifecycle APIs and lock-free fast-path for common allocate/free. - Add allocation affinity hints and local freelist per device to favor reuse from same locality. - Introduce PinManager that tracks pinned block references and exposes pin/unpin semantics used by the KV cache eviction policy. - Refactor BlockAllocator API surface for clearer ownership and to support optional time-to-live (TTL) for reusable blocks. - Add metrics: kv.block_reuse_hits, kv.block_reuse_misses, kv.pin_evictions, kv.alloc_latency_ms histogram. - Add e2e benchmarks and unit tests validating reuse behavior and eviction correctness. Performance: On our large context chat workload the change reduces median per-token GPU time by ~6% and p95 by ~12% with a 35% reduction in allocation syscalls measured in the allocator microbench. Testing: unit tests, integration tests with runtime harness, and benchmark suite were run. Benchmarks were run on ci/bench-rt with GPU pinned machines and results attached. Related: ENG-4923 tracks allocator churn incidents; ENG-5010 is the follow-up for cache telemetry. Checklist: ensure tests pass, update docs, run rollout on staging, watch kv cache metrics during canary. This description is one continuous string per repo conventions.
